messages:
Zara: Quick follow-up to the RFC: sketched three placement patterns for compatibility transforms: preprocessor (edge), in-flight adapter (runtime), model-plugin (per-model sidecar). Link to design sketch: https://redwood.internal/r/compat-placement
Nate: Short summary of pros/cons?
Zara: Preprocessor: single place to rewrite requests, easy to audit, but streaming is tricky if we need to rewrite frames. In-flight adapter: preserves streaming semantics, can act on per-model policies, but adds CPU per token. Model-plugin: local to pod, low latency for private tenants, operationally heavier to deploy and version.
Maya: We should frame the decision around two axes: streaming fidelity and operational blast radius. If streaming fidelity is required, rule out any solution that buffers full payloads at the edge.
Cheng: Agree. Another axis: cache friendliness. If we normalize whitespace/ordering at edge we may reduce cache hits for embeddings and prefix cache. We need to measure delta.
Zara: Proposal: choose hybrid default: preprocessor=opt-in tenant flag; in-flight adapter=hosted default; model-plugin=customer-managed private deployment. That lets hosted customers keep runtime control while private tenants can run their own translator.
Nate: Rollout plan sketch: 1) implement read-only shadowing at preprocessor (no rewrite) for 5d; 2) enable 1% live rewrites for low-traffic tenants; 3) expand to traffic buckets and opt-in tenants.
Maya: Metrics to instrument before rollout: rewrite_p50_latency, rewrite_p99_latency, streaming_frame_latency, embed_prefix_cache_hit, schema_mismatch_count.
Cheng: Add synthetic check: run recorded streaming sessions through the translator and verify frame sequence equality. We'll need a harness.
Zara: Fuzzing idea: mutate message arrays (insert metadata fields, change role order, add null content) and assert runtime behavior unchanged. Automate nightly.
Nate: Access control: if we accept header toggles (eg `X-Compat-Mode: rewrite|shadow|bypass`) we must validate token scopes and audit header uses. No header-based bypass for consumer tokens.
Maya: Also plan to persist tenant mapping table in config-store with versioned entries. Example entry: 
```
# config-store key: compat/model-mapping/2026-03-21
model_mappings:
  "old-model-name-1": "openvariant-v2",
  "legacy-embeds-v1": "embeds-a16-quant"
```
Cheng: Fallback semantics: prefer exact model id, else lookup mapping, else reject if tenant policy requires strict pinning. Default to best-effort mapped variant for non-critical tenants.
Zara: Console UX: show tenant opt-in state, mapping diffs, and a small "compat preview" that runs a sample request through the translator and shows diff. UX will help support triage.
Nate: Tests: unit translator tests, integration streaming smoke, and an end-to-end perf run that measures p50/p90 token latency with instrumentation on/off.
Maya: Acceptance gates before 100% rollout: p50 token latency delta < 3%, p90 < 8% for hosted; no frame reordering in streaming; embed cache hit drop < 1.5%. If any are violated, revert rewrites for that tenant.
Cheng: Ops: ensure rewrites are feature-flagged at route-level and we keep `X-Compat-Trace` injected for tracing. Audit logs for any rewrite decision stored to S3 for 30d.
ops-bot: canary deploy started: compat-preprocessor-shadow v0.3 -> canary-cluster :rocket:
Zara: Action items: Zara -> implement preprocessor shadow logic (ETA 5d), Nate -> build streaming equality harness (ETA 10d), Cheng -> config-store schema + mapping writer (ETA 3d), Maya -> update RFC and draft canary runbook.
Maya: One last point: for model-plugin we should provide a shim SDK (small library) so customers don't have to reimplement canonicalizer. Keep it minimal and MIT.
Nate: Good call. SDK should be stable v1 and document clearly which fields are safe to mutate.
Zara: Thanks all. Will post follow-up with prototype logs and early metrics. :thumbsup:
